title_en: Anti-Food Waste Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution for the purposes of preventing food waste, ensuring national food security, promoting the traditional virtues of the Chinese nation, practicing the core socialist values, conserving resources, protecting the environment, and promoting sustainable economic and social development.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "food" means food as defined in the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, including various kinds of food for human consumption or drinking.
For the purposes of this Law, "food waste" means the failure to reasonably utilize food that is safe for consumption or drinking in accordance with its functional purpose, including discarding, or causing a reduction in quantity or a decline in quality of food due to unreasonable utilization.

Article 3 The State shall practice strict economy and oppose waste.
The State shall adhere to the principles of taking multiple measures simultaneously, adopting targeted policies, conducting scientific management, and achieving social co-governance, and shall take technically feasible and economically reasonable measures to prevent and reduce food waste.
The State shall advocate civilized, healthy, resource-conserving, and environmentally friendly consumption patterns, and promote simple, moderate, green, and low-carbon lifestyles.

Article 4 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen their leadership over the work against food waste, set objectives and tasks for combating food waste, establish and improve the working mechanism for combating food waste, organize monitoring, investigation, analysis, and assessment of food waste, strengthen supervision and management, and promote the work against food waste.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall annually disclose to the public the status of food waste countermeasures, propose measures to strengthen food waste prevention, and continuously promote food waste prevention throughout society.

Article 5 The development and reform department of the State Council shall strengthen the organization and coordination of the nationwide work against food waste; together with the relevant departments of the State Council, it shall annually analyze and assess the situation of food waste, make overall arrangements for the work against food waste, and propose relevant work measures and opinions for implementation by the relevant departments.
The competent commerce department of the State Council shall strengthen the administration of the catering industry, establish and improve industry standards and service norms; together with the market supervision and administration department of the State Council and other departments, it shall establish institutional norms for combating food waste in the catering industry, and take measures to encourage catering service providers to offer individual meal services and disclose to the public their food waste prevention efforts.
The market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall strengthen supervision over food producers and traders concerning food waste prevention, and urge them to implement measures against food waste.
The national food and strategic reserves administration shall strengthen the management of grain conservation and loss reduction during storage and circulation, and together with the relevant departments of the State Council, organize the implementation of standards for grain storage, transport, and processing.
The relevant departments of the State Council shall, in accordance with this Law and their duties as prescribed by the State Council, take measures to carry out the work against food waste.

Article 6 State organs, people's organizations, and state-owned enterprises and institutions shall, in accordance with the relevant state provisions, refine and improve the meal norms for official activities such as official receptions, meetings, and training, strengthen management, and take the lead in practicing economy and opposing waste.
Where meals need to be arranged for official activities, the quantity and form of meals shall be arranged frugally according to the actual circumstances, and shall not exceed the prescribed standards.

Article 8 Entities that have canteens shall establish and improve canteen meal management systems, formulate and implement measures to prevent food waste, strengthen publicity and education, and enhance awareness of combating food waste.
Entity canteens shall strengthen dynamic management of food procurement, storage, and processing, purchase, cook, and distribute meals according to the number of diners, increase the utilization rate of raw materials and the cooking level, provide meals in accordance with the principles of health, economy, and standardization, and pay attention to dietary balance.
Entity canteens shall improve the meal service method, post or place anti-food-waste signs in conspicuous positions, and guide diners to order and take food in appropriate amounts; where wasteful behavior occurs, they shall promptly remind and correct it.

Article 9 Schools shall monitor, analyze, and assess the number and composition of diners, and strengthen the management of school canteen catering services; where off-campus meal suppliers are selected, they shall establish and improve mechanisms for introduction and withdrawal, and select the best.
School canteens and off-campus meal suppliers shall strengthen refined management, supply meals according to demand, improve meal supply methods, provide scientifically nutritious meal combinations, enrich the variety of meal sizes and flavor options, regularly listen to the opinions of diners, and ensure the quality of dishes and staple foods.

Article 10 Food delivery platforms shall, in a conspicuous manner, remind consumers to order food in appropriate quantities. Catering service providers that provide services through food delivery platforms shall, on the platform pages, provide consumers with information such as food portions, sizes, or recommended number of consumers.

Article 11 Tourism operators shall guide tourists to dine in a civilized and healthy manner. Travel agencies and tour guides shall reasonably arrange group meals, and remind tourists to order and take food in appropriate amounts. Relevant industries shall incorporate the food waste prevention efforts of tourism operators into the relevant quality standard rating indicators.

Article 12 Food business operators such as supermarkets and department stores shall strengthen daily inspections of the food they sell, manage food nearing its shelf life by category, and either make special markings or display and sell them in a centralized manner.

Article 13 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall take measures to oppose extravagance and waste, encourage and promote the holding of activities in a civilized and frugal manner, and foster an atmosphere where waste is shameful and thrift is honorable.
Where meals are needed for weddings, funerals, gatherings of friends and family, business activities, etc., the organizers and participants shall prepare and order food in moderation, and dine in a civilized and healthy manner.

Article 14 Individuals shall cultivate a civilized, healthy, rational, and green consumption concept, and when dining out, shall order and take food reasonably based on their personal health conditions, dietary habits, and dining needs.
Families and their members shall, in family life, cultivate good habits of being scientific and healthy, making the best use of things, and preventing waste, and shall purchase, store, and prepare food according to actual daily needs.

Article 15 The State shall improve the standards for the production, storage, transport, and processing of grain and other edible agricultural products, promote the use of new technologies, new techniques, and new equipment, guide moderate processing and comprehensive utilization, and reduce losses.
Food producers and traders shall take measures to improve the conditions for food storage, transport, and processing, prevent food spoilage, and reduce losses during storage and transport; increase the utilization rate of food processing, and avoid excessive processing and overuse of raw materials.

Article 16 When formulating and revising relevant national standards, industry standards, and local standards, preventing food waste shall be taken as an important consideration, and under the premise of ensuring food safety, waste shall be prevented to the greatest extent.
Food shelf life shall be set scientifically and reasonably, marked conspicuously, and easily identifiable.

Article 17 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall establish a supervision and inspection mechanism for combating food waste, and promptly urge rectification of food waste problems discovered.
Where food producers or traders seriously waste food in the course of food production and trading, the market supervision and administration, commerce, and other departments of the local people's government at or above the county level may interview their legal representatives or principal persons in charge. The food producers or traders so interviewed shall immediately make rectifications.

Article 18 The government offices administration department shall, together with the relevant departments, establish a system for evaluating and reporting the effectiveness of anti-food-waste work in government canteens, and incorporate anti-food-waste efforts into the assessment of energy and resource conservation in public institutions and the activities for creating conservation-oriented government offices.

Article 19 Food industry and catering industry associations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, formulate and implement relevant group standards and industry self-discipline norms such as those against food waste in accordance with law, publicize and popularize knowledge on preventing food waste, promote advanced models, guide their members to voluntarily carry out anti-food-waste activities, and take necessary self-discipline measures against members who engage in wasteful behavior.
Food industry and catering industry associations shall monitor food waste, strengthen analysis and assessment, annually disclose to the public the status of food waste prevention and the monitoring and assessment results, provide support for state organs in formulating laws, regulations, policies, standards and conducting research on relevant issues, and accept public supervision.
Consumers' associations and other consumer organizations shall strengthen dietary consumption education for consumers, and guide them to form consumption habits of consciously resisting waste.

Article 20 State organs, people's organizations, social organizations, enterprises, institutions, and grassroots self-governing mass organizations shall take the practice of economy and opposition to waste as part of the mass activities for promoting cultural and ethical progress, incorporate it into the relevant evaluation systems for such activities and into local civic conventions, village rules and agreements, industry norms, etc., strengthen publicity, education, and scientific popularization on combating food waste, promote the "Clean Plate Campaign", advocate civilized, healthy, and scientific dietary culture, and enhance the public's awareness of combating food waste.
People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall continuously organize and carry out publicity and education on combating food waste, and shall take combating food waste as an important part of the National Food Security Publicity Week.

Article 21 The administrative department for education shall guide and urge schools to strengthen education and management on combating food waste.
Schools shall, in accordance with regulations, conduct education on national conditions, incorporate the practice of economy and opposition to waste into educational and teaching content, and carry out special educational activities on combating food waste through learning practices, labor experiences, and other forms, to cultivate students' habits of diligence, thrift, and cherishing food.
Schools shall establish a supervision and inspection mechanism for preventing food waste, and formulate and implement corresponding reward and punishment measures.

Article 22 News media shall conduct public interest publicity on laws, regulations, relevant standards, and knowledge concerning combating food waste, report on advanced models, expose wasteful phenomena, guide the public to establish correct dietary consumption concepts, and exercise public opinion supervision over food waste behaviors. Publicity reports on combating food waste shall be truthful and fair.
It is prohibited to produce, publish, or disseminate programs or audio-visual information that promotes large-portion eating, binge eating, or other food waste behaviors.
Where a network audio-visual service provider discovers that a user has violated the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it shall immediately stop transmitting the relevant information; if the circumstances are serious, it shall stop providing information services.

Article 23 The civil affairs, market supervision and administration, and other departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a mechanism for matching donation needs, and guide food producers and traders, among others, to donate food to relevant social organizations, welfare institutions, relief agencies, or individuals, under the premise of ensuring food safety. The relevant organizations shall receive and distribute food in a timely manner according to needs.
The State encourages social forces to participate in food donation activities. Internet information service providers may build platforms to provide services such as food donation.
Article 24 Entities, households, and individuals that produce kitchen waste shall fulfill the obligation of source reduction of kitchen waste in accordance with law.

Article 25 The State organizes the monitoring of nutritional status and the popularization of nutritional knowledge, guides citizens to form scientific dietary habits, and reduces the risk of diseases caused by unhealthy diets.

Article 26 People's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to support scientific research, technological development, and other activities for preventing food waste.
Government procurement of relevant goods and services shall be conducive to preventing food waste.
The State implements tax policies that favor the prevention of food waste.

Article 27 Any entity or individual that discovers food waste behaviors by food producers or traders or others shall have the right to report to relevant departments and authorities. The departments and authorities that receive such reports shall handle them in a timely manner in accordance with law.

Article 28 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a catering service provider fails to proactively remind consumers to prevent food waste, the market supervision and administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level or the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and give it a warning.
Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a catering service provider induces or misleads consumers into ordering excessive amounts of food, causing obvious waste, the market supervision and administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level or the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and give it a warning; if it refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan shall be imposed.
Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a food producer or trader causes serious food waste in the course of food production and trading, the market supervision and administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level or the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections; if it refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 29 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, an entity that has a canteen fails to formulate or implement measures to prevent food waste, the department designated by the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections and give it a warning.

Article 30 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a radio station, television station, or network audio-visual service provider produces, publishes, or disseminates programs or audio-visual information that promotes large-portion eating, binge eating, or other food waste behaviors, the radio and television, cyberspace administration, or other relevant departments shall, within their respective responsibilities, order it to make corrections and give it a warning; if it refuses to make corrections or if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed, and it may be ordered to suspend relevant business or suspend operations for rectification; the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be investigated for legal liability in accordance with law.

Article 31 Provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, or cities divided into districts and autonomous prefectures may, based on their specific circumstances and actual needs, formulate specific measures for combating food waste in their respective regions.
Article 32 This Law shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
